full_judgment:
7. Mr Abdus Salam Mamun, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner, submits that the present accused-petitioner being a contractor is not a public servant, and, as such, the impugned proceeding initiated against the accused-petitioner under sections 409/109 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable in the eye of law. Learned Advocate, in support of his, submissions, has relied on the decisions in the cases of State vs Iqbal Hossain reported in 48 DLR (AD) 100, Khurshid Alam vs Azizur Rahman reported in 9 BLC (AD) 241, Md Joiatiur Rahman vs State reported in 19 BLD 607 = 4 BLC 375, Golam (Md) Abdul Awal Sarkar vs State reported in 49 DLR 95, Abul Basher vs State reported in 47 DLR 521, Abdul Ali vs State reported in 30 DLR (SC) 58, and Taslima Khatoon Chhanda vs State, reported in 17 BLC 277. He next submits that there are 3 accused in the present case and out of 3 accused, accused No.1 Col. Oli Ahmed was. the then Minister, but the case lodged against him was withdrawn by the Government and learned Divisional Special Judge accorded permission to the withdrawal of the case and the case initiated against another accused Md Nurul Anowar, Chairman of Harala Union Parishad was quashed by a Division Bench of this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9804 of2003, and, as such, there is no public servant in this case at present, and, as such, the proceeding pending against accused Md Yunus, the Chairman of Harala Union Parishad, who is admittedly not a public servant is not maintainable in the eye of law. He then submits that since no money or property was not entrusted to the accused-petitioner, the question of committing the offence of criminal breach of trust does not arise at all, and, as such, the proceeding brought against the accused-petitioner under section 409 is not maintainable. In support of his contentions, he has relied on the decisions in the cases of Lutfar Rahman vs State reported in 25 DLR (AD) 101, Md Moslem Uddin vs State reported in 10 MLR 199, Rafique (Md) vs Syed Morshed Hossain reported in 50 DLR (AD) 163, Lutfar Rahman vs State reported in 21 DLR 933, He points out that the proceeding against one of the 3 accused was withdrawn and the proceeding against another accused was quashed by this Court, and under this circumstances, the impugned proceeding pending only against the present accused-petitioner, the contractor as abettor is not maintainable in the eye of law. The learned Advocate, in support of his contentions, has referred to the decision in the case of Moyna Miali vs State reported in 5 BLD (AD) 99. Learned Advocate for the petitioner opposing the submission of the learned Advocate for opposite party No.2, has added that the impugned proceeding may be quashed even after framing of charge and also after conclusion of the trial of the case if circumstances demand. Learned Advocate, in support of his submissions, has referred to the decisions in the cases of OK-Kyunm-Ok vs State reported in 18 BLC 621, Taslima Khatoon Chhanda vs State reported in 17 BLC 277, State vs Md Nasim reported in 57 DLR (AD) 114, Sher Ali (Md) vs State reported in 46 DLR (AD) 67, Moudud Ahmed vs State reported in 48 DLR (AD) 42. He further submits that since the prosecution materials do not disclose any ingredients of entrustment and fraudulent mens rea to deceive the Government, and, as such, considering all the aspects of the case, the impugned proceeding initiated against the accused-petitioner should be quashed. Mr Mamun lastly submits that since the accused-petitioner is a contractor and that he is not a public servant, the Divisional special Judge has got no jurisdiction to hold trial against him under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code, which are not schedule offences of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, and, as such, the impugned proceeding is of without jurisdiction, that is, coram non-judice, and, as such, the impugned proceeding should be quashed at this moment 

 13. Similar view on the principles and categories of cases for quashing the proceedings was, earlier, followed in the decision in the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury vs State, 28 DLR (AD) 38. 

 16. It is pertinent to note that inherent power under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure can be invoked at any stage of the case even after conclusion of trial if it is necessary to prevent the abuse of the Court or otherwise to secure ends of justice. In the case of Sher Ali (Md) vs State, 46 DLR (AD) 57, it has been decided that the inherent power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure can be exercised to quash a proceeding or even a conviction on conclusion of a trial if the Court concerned got no jurisdiction to hold the said trial or the facts alleged against the accused do not constitute any criminal offence or the conviction has been based on no evidence, or otherwise to secure ends of justice. As per submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the proceeding under section 561A is maintainable even after framing of charge. On the question of maintainability of the proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the legal decisions referred to by the learned Advocate' for the petitioner are squarely applicable to the instant case in hand. We find considerable force in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner on the point of maintainability. 

 17. Considering the settled propositions of law as enunciated in the decision in the case of Sher Ali (Md) vs State reported in 46 DLR (AD) 67, we are of the view that the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the accused-petitioner is maintainable even after framing of charge.
